summary: Plan a read-only Opus 4.8 review to identify the scope and risks of existing Ctrl/IME-related changes without modifying repository files or inspecting excluded paths.
assumptions: The requested work is a review/scope-identification task, not an implementation task.
Only existing changed files that are clearly related to Ctrl key handling, IME input, soft keyboard behavior, terminal input dispatch, or associated tests should be reviewed.
Ambiguous changed files should be skipped and recorded as out of scope rather than broadly inspected.
Opus 4.8 is the requested review model/provider target.

tasks.title: Identify Ctrl/IME Change Scope
tasks.description: Use only read-only git metadata commands such as `git status --short`, `git diff --name-only`, and narrowly targeted `git diff -- <path>` for non-excluded paths that are clearly related to Ctrl key handling, IME input, soft keyboard behavior, terminal input dispatch, or associated tests. Do not modify, create, delete, rename, move, or type-change any repository paths. Do not run denied commands or denied git operations. Record the reviewed file list, skipped ambiguous files, relevant findings, and any residual review gaps.
verification: Confirm the reviewed file list is limited to clearly Ctrl/IME-related changes.
Confirm no excluded paths were listed, searched, opened, summarized, transmitted, created, or modified.
Confirm Opus 4.8 is the requested review model/provider target.
Confirm only read-only git metadata and targeted diff commands were used.

risks: Changed file names alone may not be enough to determine Ctrl/IME relevance, causing some ambiguous changes to be skipped.
A Ctrl/IME behavior regression could exist in a file whose path does not clearly indicate input, keyboard, terminal dispatch, or tests.
Read-only review cannot validate behavior by changing code or adding tests.
